description: We are a small team of beginners brought together by a shared curiosity about space exploration. While we are still new to coding and learning the ropes, we are excited to build our skills, tackle starter space projects, and learn as we go.
summary: ASTROBASE is a free browser game that lets kids aged 7 to 12 run their own Mars base. The player is a junior astronaut who lands on Mars, builds a small colony, and keeps the crew alive: balancing oxygen, water, food, energy and crew health while dust storms, oxygen leaks and radiation warnings test every decision. It directly answers the challenge: a playable game where young learners manage a Martian outpost and feel first-hand how life support, power, food production and shelter decide whether a mission succeeds or fails. It runs in any browser with no download, no account and no cost, on desktop and mobile, and it works offline once loaded.
details: ASTROBASE: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer — Build Your Base. Protect Your Crew. Explore Mars. 1. Project Functionality and Core Mechanics ASTROBASE: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based 2D pixel-art Mars colony survival and resource-management game designed specifically for young learners and beginners. Rather than presenting space science as a passive slideshow, the application immerses players in a complete, hands-on simulation where they take on the role of a junior astronaut tasked with establishing and sustaining a human settlement on the Martian surface. Exploration and Construction: Players navigate an astronaut across a top-down Martian landscape, complete with craters, rocky terrain, and a landing zone, to inspect sites and construct essential life-support infrastructure on a placement grid. Resource Management: Players continuously balance five core survival metrics measured in child-friendly game units: Oxygen, Water, Food, Energy, and Crew Health. Buildings dynamically generate or consume these resources. Turn-Based Day Simulation: Gameplay progresses through an End Day cycle. At the conclusion of each Martian sol (day), the engine computes net production and consumption, updates crew health, advances ongoing construction or research, evaluates mission milestones, triggers environmental events, and generates an itemized Daily Report. 2. Key Benefits Experiential STEM Learning: Translates abstract aerospace and planetary survival concepts, such as closed-loop life support, solar power generation, in-situ water extraction, greenhouse agriculture, and radiation shielding, into tangible cause-and-effect gameplay decisions. Zero-Friction Accessibility: Engineered as a lightweight web application that runs directly in standard browsers across desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices without requiring software installations, user accounts, or paid subscriptions. Persistent Local Progress: Utilizes browser-native storage to automatically save and restore game states, mission completions, and achievements offline while offering safe reset confirmations and graceful recovery from corrupted data. 3. Intended Impact The primary goal of ASTROBASE is to spark early curiosity in space exploration, environmental sustainability, and systems thinking among young students. By presenting resource interdependence and problem-solving in an encouraging, low-barrier format, while explicitly distinguishing simplified game mechanics from real-world aerospace engineering, the project builds foundational scientific literacy and strategic reasoning skills in an approachable way. 4. Tools, Languages, Hardware, and Software Stack Core Languages: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript — application structure, responsive layout, core game loop and state logic. Graphics and Audio: HTML5 Canvas 2D, Web Audio API — procedural pixel-art terrain, astronaut and building rendering, animations, and optional synthesized sound effects. Data Persistence: Browser LocalStorage — client-side autosaving, manual continuation, settings storage, and progress tracking. Development and Hosting: Google AI Studio workflow, GitHub Pages — structured iterative development and static web deployment via relative paths. Target Hardware: Desktops, laptops, tablets, smartphones — cross-device compatibility supporting both physical keyboards and touchscreens. 5. Creative Design Elements Cohesive Retro Pixel-Art World: Uses procedural Canvas 2D pixel-art techniques to render warm red-orange Martian topography, distinct functional structures (Habitat, Solar Panel, Oxygen Generator, Greenhouse, Water Extractor, and Research Laboratory), and visual production indicators without external graphic assets. Progressive Narrative Campaign: Structures learning around a five-stage mission arc — Establish the Base, Secure Water, Grow Food on Mars, Scientific Research, and Survive the Dust Storm — giving players clear objectives, unlock sequences, and rewards. Dynamic Environmental Hazards: Introduces interactive emergencies, including dust storms that reduce solar efficiency, oxygen leaks, water shortages, power failures, and solar radiation warnings requiring shelter, to keep gameplay engaging and educational. 6. Key Design and Engineering Considerations Age-Appropriate Cognitive Load: Interfaces are kept clean and uncluttered, resource values are prevented from dropping into confusing negative numbers, and every hazard or building includes concise, plain-language explanations detailing what occurred and how to respond. Cross-Platform Input and Layout Responsiveness: Supports desktop keyboard navigation (WASD and Arrow keys) alongside mobile-friendly virtual directional controls, touch-based grid placement, and zoom-safe responsive panels. Deployment Reliability and Offline Resilience: Enforces a strict static-site architecture with zero external API calls, ensuring that the game functions reliably in classrooms or homes with intermittent internet connectivity and can be hosted effortlessly on static platforms.
